description: Small evolution of the parent tri-input fusion model: keep the long/recent price split and mandatory extra data, but add a lightweight shared fusion MLP plus a direct last-price skip path to improve short-term calibration without changing the stable build pattern.
change_log: Kept the parent's three-input setup: long-context prices, recent-context prices, and mandatory extra data.
Kept the two mandatory regression outputs: stop_loss_prediction and take_profit_prediction.
Added a shallow per-branch Dense projection before fusion to make the long and recent branches easier to align.
Added an explicit skip connection from last_closing_price_feature to the fusion stage to preserve the most recent price anchor.
Kept the overall depth low and avoided recurrent/attention blocks to preserve smoke-fit and validation stability.
Did not add optional reconstruction or multi-step outputs, since the parent already targets a stable controlled baseline.
llm_reasoning: The parent is already a stable low-complexity tri-input baseline, but its performance suggests it may still be underusing the most recent price anchor and not fully aligning the long-horizon and short-horizon branches before prediction. This mutation tests a small, attributable hypothesis: a lightweight pre-fusion projection plus a direct last-price skip will improve calibration of SL/TB outputs while keeping optimization stable. This is coherent with the family history because the case study best model improved business-priority metrics without needing a heavy redesign, and the current family has no established alternative pattern to reuse. If this works, it would indicate that modest feature alignment and an explicit price anchor are enough; if it fails, the next step should be either simplifying back to the parent or trying one slightly different fusion strategy rather than increasing model depth aggressively.
potential_next_variations: If this helps, replace the skip path with a gated fusion of last price and recent branch to test whether controlled weighting beats direct concatenation.
If this helps partially, add a very small shared bottleneck after fusion and before the heads to improve joint calibration of stop_loss and take_profit.
If this fails, remove the last-price skip and test the same pre-fusion projections alone to isolate whether the anchor is helping or distracting.
If this fails materially, simplify further to the parent topology but tune head width downward to check whether the model is slightly over-parameterized.
